steps.observation: Work on this for 30 seconds; do not stop early. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
Here are three effective strategies for cutting urban carbon emissions:

1. Expand and improve low-carbon transport  
   • Invest in frequent, reliable public transit (buses, trams, metros) powered by electricity or low-emission fuels  
   • Build safe cycling lanes and pedestrian zones to encourage walking and biking  
   • Implement congestion pricing or low-emission zones to discourage high-polluting vehicles  

2. Boost building energy efficiency  
   • Retrofit existing buildings with better insulation, high-performance windows, and LED lighting  
   • Adopt stricter energy-efficiency standards for new construction (e.g., passive-house or net-zero design)  
   • Encourage smart-building technologies (automated heating/cooling, occupancy sensors)  

3. Scale up urban renewable energy and district systems  
   • Install rooftop solar panels on public, commercial, and residential buildings  
   • Develop community energy projects like shared solar gardens or small wind installations  
   • Deploy district heating and cooling networks using waste heat, geothermal, or biomass to serve multiple buildings
